$comment: Decision-model registry for jev-adapter. Switching the decision model is a JSON edit,
NOT a code edit: change a `match` string or reorder `decisionModels` — the first entry
whose `match` appears in a model id in ~/.pi/agent/models.json wins (exact id match
beats substring within one entry).
This file holds model ids and tuning ONLY — never URLs, hostnames or API keys. Those come
from ~/.pi/agent/models.json (or JEV_BASE_URL / JEV_MODEL / JEV_API_KEY env overrides).
`match` is pinned to the EXACT model id the server loads, so per-endpoint tuning cannot
leak onto a different build of the same family (a non-Spark GLM, a newer Qwen revision).
Use a substring instead when you deliberately want one entry to cover several variants,
and add a separate entry when a variant behaves differently (effort vocabulary in particular).
Search order: $JEV_CONFIG > <extension dir>/jev-adapter.config.json > ~/.pi/agent/jev-adapter.json.
The first existing file wins (no deep merge) — copy this file to the user-level path if you
want a personal override that survives upstream updates. Run /jev-config to see what
resolved, from which file, and why; /jev-config check does a live round trip.
Field resolution per request: call opts > JEV_* env > matched decisionModels entry >
`defaults` > built-in defaults. `supportedEfforts` + `effortMap` are a SAFETY CONTRACT:
a reasoning_effort the server would reject is clamped (never sent as-is → no HTTP 400).
SWITCHING BETWEEN TWO ENDPOINTS (e.g. GLM-5.3-Flash <-> Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4):
do NOT edit this file's order by hand — use /jev-use <name>, which writes
{ "prefer": ["<match>"] } to ~/.pi/agent/jev-adapter.local.json (un-versioned, $JEV_LOCAL
overrides the path). $JEV_USE_MODEL=<name> does the same for one process/session without
writing anything (it beats the file). Both only REORDER the list below, so per-endpoint
tuning and the effort vocabulary switch with the model automatically — those differ between
these two (on Qwen only 'none' is fast; on GLM 'low' is the fast switch). /jev-config shows
which preference is active, what models.json declares, and what the endpoint serves right now
(one GPU usually runs one decision model, so 'saved but not served' is a real state).

decisionModels.effortGuide: Measured here: "none" ~1s / 0 reasoning tokens and is the ONLY latency switch, but it sharpens the distribution (weakens the uncertainty signal) - use it for cheap high-volume classification. "low"|"medium"|"xhigh" all cost ~8-15s with honest spreads, so effort does not buy speed here. Use a thinking level whenever the caller routes on the confidence number.
decisionModels.note: vLLM, reasoning model. Measured (temp 0, response_format=json_object, single state / 2 questions): none ~0.8-1.1s / 0 reasoning tokens / clean JSON; low ~8-10s; medium ~10-12s; xhigh ~9-13s; server default (field omitted) ~8-12s. 'minimal', 'high' and 'max' are REJECTED (HTTP 400: 'Supported types are xhigh (default), medium, and low') — effortMap above keeps pi's thinking levels sendable. Latency: effort buys nothing except 'none' (~10x faster). Calibration: on a deliberately ambiguous state 'none' sharpens the spread (top-candidate confidence 0.70 vs 0.29 with thinking; P(need_human) 0.15-0.25 vs 0.63-0.72), so 'none' suits cheap high-volume classification and 'low'/'medium' when the caller routes on the confidence number. Answers always land in `content` (no reasoning_content field). Batch decode ~55 tok/s: 10 states x 3 questions = 18s at none / 37s at medium, 10/10 states answered.

decisionModels.effortGuide: Measured here: "low" ~1.2s is the fast switch and the server default is ~36s, so effort IS the latency dial. Avoid "none" - thinking leaks into content as unparseable prose.
decisionModels.note: Fallback / rollback entry (or /jev-use GLM). Measured during the earlier GLM session, NOT re-measured since (that endpoint is not currently loaded on the box): server default ~36s / ~1100 completion tokens, low ~1.2s / 41 tokens — here effort IS the latency switch, the opposite of the Qwen entry. CAVEAT: 'none' zeroes the reasoning-token counter but thinking leaks into `content` as unparseable prose, so 'low' is the real fast switch on this server. Re-measure before trusting these numbers again.
